title: Finite presentation over a qcqs space has qcqs source
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Point spaces carry the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. An algebraic space is quasi-compact if its point space is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover); it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme mapping to its target has quasi-compact point space; it is quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism, where $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Suppose $f$ is of finite presentation, meaning quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

proof.text: First extend the affine-test definition of quasi-compactness to quasi-compact space tests. Let $h:A\to B$ satisfy that definition, and let $C\to B$ have quasi-compact point space. By [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas], choose an affine scheme $U$ with a surjective etale map $U\to C$. The space $A\times_BU$ has quasi-compact point space by the hypothesis on $h$. The projection $A\times_BU\to A\times_BC$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the fibre-product universal property. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] its point map is continuous and surjective. For any open cover of $|A\times_BC|$, inverse images cover $|A\times_BU|$; a finite subcover upstairs covers downstairs by surjectivity. Thus $|A\times_BC|$ is quasi-compact. Conversely arbitrary quasi-compact space tests include affine schemes, which are quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

source.place: Tag 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local), proof of (3) implies (1); spaces-properties.tex Tags 03H6 and 03BX.

proof.text: Quasi-compact morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change and composition in the affine-test convention. For $h:A\to B$, $B'\to B$ and affine $T\to B'$, the test of the base change is $(A\times_BB')\times_{B'}T\cong A\times_BT$, so it is quasi-compact. For quasi-compact $A\to B\to C$ and affine $T\to C$, first $B\times_CT$ is quasi-compact; step 1 then shows $A\times_B(B\times_CT)$ quasi-compact. This is $A\times_CT$. Both identifications send compatible tuples to the same components and have inverses inserting the uniquely prescribed component, so follow directly from the sheaf fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. These are two-line consequences of step 1 and the definitions, rather than additional lemmas to be added to the DAG.

source.place: Tags 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact) and 03HG (lemma-composition-quasi-compact), the omitted transitivity-of-fibre-products arguments.

proof.text: Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness of $f$ by the hypothesis as stated. Apply step 1 with $A=X$, $B=C=Y$ and $C\to B$ the identity. Its conclusion is that $|X\times_YY|=|X|$ is quasi-compact. The identification sends $(x,f(x))$ to $x$, with inverse $x\mapsto(x,f(x))$, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. This proves the quasi-compactness clause without using local finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 06G5 (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), quasi-compactness clause, expanded using Tag 03KG.

proof.text: Put $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and regard the given spaces as absolute spaces, as in the definition of quasi-separatedness in the statement. The map $k:X\times_YX\to X\times_ZX$ is the pullback of $\Delta_{Y/Z}:Y\to Y\times_ZY$ along $f\times f$. Indeed a section of that pullback consists of $(x_1,x_2,y)$ with $f(x_1)=y=f(x_2)$, equivalent to the pair $(x_1,x_2)$ defining $X\times_YX$; the inverse inserts $y=f(x_1)$. These maps commute with restrictions, so this is an isomorphism of sheaves, hence of the algebraic-space fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Since $Y$ is quasi-separated, $\Delta_{Y/Z}$ is quasi-compact; step 2 makes $k$ quasi-compact. Since $f$ is quasi-separated, $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_YX$ is quasi-compact. Their composite is $\Delta_{X/Z}$, because both send $x$ to $(x,x)$. Step 2 makes this composite quasi-compact. By the stated definition $X$ is quasi-separated, proving the second clause. No separation property of the ambient $S$ was used.

tool_uses.why: Only general existence, universal property, and etale base change of algebraic-space fibre products are used; no trace formula, pairing, duality, or cohomology argument.

lean.statement: theorem qcqs_source_of_finitePresentation {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hYqc : CompactSpace (Point Y.obj.obj)) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated Y) (hfqc : MapIsQuasiCompact f.hom.hom) (hfqs : MapIsQuasiCompact (pullback.diagonal f.hom.hom)) (hflfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f) : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj) ∧ IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X
lean.note: Point-space compactness uses the existing atlas topology. Absolute quasi-separatedness uses the existing equivalent affine-test predicate, without any assumption on S. Finite presentation is expanded into the three specified hypotheses using the landed predicates; no new notion or dependency module is introduced.

Conclusion: CompactSpace (Point X) ∧ IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X. Nothing extra assumed (no instance, universe equality, separatedness of S or representability of f).
